messages.body_plain:
Hi Dirk,

On Wed, 2013-05-01 at 13:46 -0500, Dirk Eddelbuettel wrote:
[...]
> Of course, but there are a few notable exceptions. Boost regex is one, and
> the system / error code library you have here is another.

And I need both...

I just created an 
	rforge/boostheaders/BoostHeadersROOT/src/Makevars

with 

	OBJECTS=\
	../inst/include/libs/system/src/error_code.o \
	[...]
	../inst/include/libs/regex/src/regex.o \
	../inst/include/libs/regex/src/wide_posix_api.o \
	[...]

	PKG_CPPFLAGS=-I ../inst/include

and upon R CMD INSTALL BH I got an
/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/BH/libs/BH.so


> We can't help with that as this would get us towards the need for linking,
> configure, ... and all that.
So far I got away without any need for configure.
The mzR package then uses PKG_LDFLAGS to link th BH.so into mzR.so

My main problem at the moment is to get all boost headers
required for mzR into BH without copying *all* of boost,
which I do with a very ugly 

	system  (paste('find /vol/R/BioC/devel-29/mzR/src/pwiz -type f ',
            '-exec bcp --scan --boost=', boostroot,
            ' {}  ', 
            pkgdir, '/inst/include \\; >> bcp.log ', sep=''))

That'd need a bit of streamlining. My work-in-progress can be found at 

	https://github.com/sneumann/mzR/tree/BH
and	https://github.com/sneumann/boostheaders

Caveat, the boostheaders will create a BH with 1.43.0,
because the current mzR / pwiz code won't work with 1.51.0 ...

What do you think ?

Yours,
Steffen

The package is also on CRAN.

What Steffen did not mention is that it is _template headers only_ based on
the good experience we had with Armadillo and Eigen headers from R/Rcpp. So
that brings potentially quite a lot of Boost to R, but not all of Boost.

Reges, Graph, Date formatting/parsing, ... all need object code too, and are
thus not fully helped by package BH.
 
| I know a few packages on BioC are using -- and embedding -- boost.

Same on CRAN.  Our argument of providing all / most of these in one package
to be used at compile-time was apparently good enough for the CRAN
maintainers to accept it.

Now we just need to make it better.

messages.subject: [Boostheaders-devel] [Bioc-devel] Boost packaged on rforge
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

BH currently works the way that the package sources 
(and that includes BH/inst/include/boost/*) are 
automagically created by bcp'ing the dependencies 
of *some* R packages (e.g. bigmemory on rforge).

John and Dirk et al said that people can ask 
for additional dependencies on the tracker [1].

If you want to port your package to BH 
and figure out the required dependencies,
check out svn://r-forge.r-project.org/svnroot/boostheaders
and edit boostheaders/CreateBoost.R (see how I munged 
that file on [2] ...)

Then iterate over 

	cd boostheaders
	rm -rf pkg/BH  
	R --vanilla <CreateBoost.R
	R CMD INSTALL pkg/BH
	R CMD INSTALL /your/package/

until success. Unfortunately with boost, it might not 
be as straightforward as adding " graph ",
that's why I have that insane "find /my/package -exec bcp -scan"
in my hacked [2]. Also note that in a hacked version of 
CreateBoost.R it is possible to switch between boost versions.

Yours,
Steffen


[1] https://r-forge.r-project.org/tracker/?atid=5310&group_id=1469&func=browse
[2] https://github.com/sneumann/boostheaders/blob/master/CreateBoost.R

Our thought process is/was that there are lots of packages that use only a

in one or two packages that apply, but Jay and Mike drove the concrete first
build of BH by providing what bigmemory needed.

RBGL may be pushing it, but we would surely try to accomodate it, provided
this would work without linking.  We really want to try to limit ourselves to
templates here.

On 1 May 2013 at 23:06, Steffen Neumann wrote:
| Hi Dirk,
| 
| On Wed, 2013-05-01 at 13:46 -0500, Dirk Eddelbuettel wrote:
| [...]
| > Of course, but there are a few notable exceptions. Boost regex is one, and
| > the system / error code library you have here is another.
| 
| And I need both...
| 
| I just created an 
| 	rforge/boostheaders/BoostHeadersROOT/src/Makevars
| 
| with 
| 
| 	OBJECTS=\
| 	../inst/include/libs/system/src/error_code.o \
| 	[...]
| 	../inst/include/libs/regex/src/regex.o \
| 	../inst/include/libs/regex/src/wide_posix_api.o \
| 	[...]
| 
| 	PKG_CPPFLAGS=-I ../inst/include
| 
| and upon R CMD INSTALL BH I got an
| /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/BH/libs/BH.so

Interesting. 

In a way related to how Rcpp also provides its libRcpp.{a,so}.  But recall
that the system linker cannot link against BH.so (you need libBH.so) and that
from having R dynamically load BH we won't yet get the symbols resolved at
package compile/link time.

Also, what I am a little afraid of is ... us dropping the 'configure' step so
that we may silently end up with 32 / 64 bit mixups etc pp (as we're not
using Boost properly installed but just copied).  But we already do that now
so it may not get worse. 
 
| > We can't help with that as this would get us towards the need for linking,
| > configure, ... and all that.
| So far I got away without any need for configure.
| The mzR package then uses PKG_LDFLAGS to link th BH.so into mzR.so

How?  With -LBH.so?

| My main problem at the moment is to get all boost headers
| required for mzR into BH without copying *all* of boost,
| which I do with a very ugly 
| 
| 	system  (paste('find /vol/R/BioC/devel-29/mzR/src/pwiz -type f ',
|             '-exec bcp --scan --boost=', boostroot,
|             ' {}  ', 
|             pkgdir, '/inst/include \\; >> bcp.log ', sep=''))
|
| That'd need a bit of streamlining. My work-in-progress can be found at 
| 
| 	https://github.com/sneumann/mzR/tree/BH
| and	https://github.com/sneumann/boostheaders

I may not have time to play, sadly.

Dirk
 
| Caveat, the boostheaders will create a BH with 1.43.0,
| because the current mzR / pwiz code won't work with 1.51.0 ...
| 
| What do you think ?

messages.body_plain:
To extend this thread a little:

i)   I put a little bit of time the BH package and extended the package,
     trying to address the open issues at 
       https://r-forge.r-project.org/tracker/?atid=5310&group_id=1469&func=browse
     (which, sadly, Steffen never seems to have found, but I added his issue)

ii)  Now 'foreach' (#2527) and 'math/dist.' (#2533, also needed 'algorithm')
     are included.

iii) I can now build bigmemory, RcppBDT, and ExactNumCI (the driver for #2533)
     even when 'hiding' my /usr/include/boost/ -- so package BH works here!

     (Both RcppBDT and ExactNumCI, as currently on CRAN, need LinkingTo: BH,
     of course, and note that ExactNumCI has a bug in src/Makefile: remove
     BOOSTLIB which is eg unset on my system and breaks the build; I'll talk
     to them in due course.) 

iv)  Steffen's wish was added as ticket #2768 and has been addressed,
     iostream is in as well but I didn't test mzR yet

I think we are crouching towards a BH release 1.51.0-1 and I'd love for
anybody else to test a little.

Dirk

-- 
Dirk Eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org | http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com
